findings.title: Restore the 30%/70% shades for embedded-post author links
findings.body: The original author-link color used 30% lightness, but this replacement uses 70% for light themes and 30% for dark themes. Both branches now give these small author links the much dimmer shade: a black/white palette produces #b3b3b3 on white or #4d4d4d on black, with only about 2:1–2.5:1 contrast. Preserve 30% in the light branch and use 70% in the dark branch, as the regular post-author links do.

findings.title: Update the badge foreground along with its dark-theme background
findings.body: The base notification badge still sets its text color to $secondary, including the [href] variant. Changing its dark-theme background to scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%) therefore puts dark text on another dark color. With a black secondary color, the 11px count becomes black on #4d4d4d, approximately 2.5:1 contrast, whereas the previous light background kept it legible. Badges using this base background need a contrasting dark-theme foreground as well.

findings.title: Preserve the original topic-map heading shade
findings.body: This changes the light-theme topic-map heading from 20% lightness to 50%, rather than only adding a dark-theme alternative. These headings are normal-weight, normal-size text on a near-white topic-map background; for a #222 primary and white secondary, the new shade is approximately #919191 and has only about 3:1 contrast. Retain 20% for light themes and use the complementary 80% for dark themes, matching the desktop heading rule.

findings.title: Keep group-member names at their original contrast level
findings.body: The group-member name previously used 30% lightness, but the new light branch uses 50%. The same change appears in app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/user.scss at line 497. This unnecessarily reduces the contrast of normal-size member names in light themes: with a #222 primary and white secondary, it changes approximately #646464 to #919191, dropping contrast from about 5.9:1 to 3.2:1. Preserve the 30% light-theme value and use 70% for its dark-theme counterpart instead of copying the title's 50% shade.
